rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: The One Who Lets You Win
card.instruction: Return to the familiar role of making victory easier for others, then let the cost of that generosity become impossible to ignore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've left my queen where you can take it. Same as last Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want to beat you properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can. I've also stopped practising so you can catch up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then come back to chess club with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. But introduce me as your old coach. They only know me as the person you keep beating.

card.title: The One Who Lets You Win
card.instruction: Return to the familiar role of making victory easier for others, then let the cost of that generosity become impossible to ignore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've given you the good sales figures again. I'll explain the missing budget.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could split the difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You need a clean run at promotion. I can survive another meeting as the budget problem.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me introduce your section, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Say I'm explaining the hole, not that I dug it. Last time that distinction cost me a bonus.

card.title: Debts on the Scoreboard
card.instruction: Treat past wins and losses as debts. Let each new result change who owes the next favor, risk, or concession.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You beat me at darts yesterday, so you owe me lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. But you've just beaten me today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lunch cancels out. I owe you dessert for winning by more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Make it takeaway. I have to collect Mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll collect her. A three-dart finish ought to cover a parent, not just a pudding.

card.title: Debts on the Scoreboard
card.instruction: Treat past wins and losses as debts. Let each new result change who owes the next favor, risk, or concession.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You won our tennis match, so you owe me first choice of film.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You won the rematch this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's your choice. Apparently I spent two hours earning your submarine documentary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Three hours. It's a trilogy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll watch all three. But if you beat me tomorrow, you owe me the director's commentary on my musical.

card.title: Victory Without You
card.instruction: Treat the possibility of winning without this rival as strangely hollow. Keep raising the challenge so the relationship survives the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't concede. Who else am I supposed to beat at chess on Tuesdays?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've beaten me four times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Next game I start without my queen. Make me earn it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd still lose. Just take the trophy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take both my rooks too. I'm not spending Tuesdays alone with something that can't gloat.

card.title: Victory Without You
card.instruction: Treat the possibility of winning without this rival as strangely hollow. Keep raising the challenge so the relationship survives the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't retire from the bake-off. Nobody else knows when my icing is smug.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm bored with sponge cakes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then wedding cakes. Three tiers each. Give me something to fear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I made those professionally for twenty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five tiers, then, and you choose the fillings. I'd rather lose sleep over you than win another sponge nobody insults properly.

card.title: The Unfinished Rematch
card.instruction: Treat the present as another round of a contest, bargain, or failure that never reached a satisfying conclusion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we choose this year's holiday, settle who won the map argument in Cornwall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was fifteen years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. We've given the evidence ample time to mature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we just book somewhere?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After we establish who is allowed to navigate the website.

card.title: The Unfinished Rematch
card.instruction: Treat the present as another round of a contest, bargain, or failure that never reached a satisfying conclusion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Same board game, same disputed last move. I've kept the pieces exactly where they were.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've both moved house since then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The game hasn't. It's been waiting responsibly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather start again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Begin by retracting your objection to the old ending.

card.title: Winning Looks Natural on You
card.instruction: Treat the ease and confidence success seems to give others as both inspiring and threatening, then sharpen your need to outperform them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked so casual collecting that prize. I'll collect mine without even standing fully up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't won one yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm preparing a more effortless response.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're practising it in a mirror.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only until it looks less prepared than yours.

card.title: Winning Looks Natural on You
card.instruction: Treat the ease and confidence success seems to give others as both inspiring and threatening, then sharpen your need to outperform them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How do you finish five miles looking so relaxed? I'll do six smiling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm exhausted. I just save my breath for the hill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll save enough to congratulate you at the top.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can walk it together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I'll jog ahead and find us a bench. You make recovery look easy; I could have it ready for you.

card.title: Back When I Was Ahead
card.instruction: Interpret the present through a time when you felt more successful, admired, or certain of your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring back the old quiz questions. I won three years running with those.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We all remember the answers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it would reward loyalty as well as knowledge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You just want to win again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want the quiz to rediscover its standards.

card.title: Back When I Was Ahead
card.instruction: Interpret the present through a time when you felt more successful, admired, or certain of your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This old sales chart shows what I'm capable of.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's from before we sold online.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's take the website down for a fair comparison.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Most customers use it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They never gave my telephone manner a chance.

card.title: Second Place Feels Like Disappearing
card.instruction: Treat every comparison as a threat to your worth. Respond by proving that you still matter before the moment can move on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before announcing first place, could you say my name again with 'second'?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Second is a wonderful result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use my name in that sentence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Congratulations, Alex. You came second.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Keep looking this way while they fetch the bigger trophy.

card.title: Second Place Feels Like Disappearing
card.instruction: Treat every comparison as a threat to your worth. Respond by proving that you still matter before the moment can move on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You put the winning photograph above mine. Can people still see mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is right beside the light switch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So everyone touches that wall. Good.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's not a competition for attention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nobody will mind if I stand beside it answering questions.

card.title: Your Risk, My Cost
card.instruction: Treat every choice around you as a risk whose consequences may land on you. Press for a voice in decisions you cannot control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you teach the dog to fetch glasses, can I vote? I buy the glasses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my training experiment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And my experiment is making rent after the breakages.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll clean up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Include replacing the glasses in your definition of clean.

card.title: Your Risk, My Cost
card.instruction: Treat every choice around you as a risk whose consequences may land on you. Press for a voice in decisions you cannot control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thirty people camping in our garden? I maintain that lawn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only one weekend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Followed by six Saturdays of reseeding. I want a say in tent placement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Put them wherever you like, but leave room for the fire pit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I need a say in that too. You've given me the seating plan for my next repair job.

card.title: Worth Keeping Around
card.instruction: Seek signs that your contribution still earns a place. Increase your effort whenever belonging feels uncertain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've fixed your gate. Shall I come next Sunday and do the gutter?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come for lunch. My brother's doing the gutter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I'll mend those dining chairs so there's room for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's already a chair for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll check the table legs. I'd like my place here to be something you can rely on.

card.title: Worth Keeping Around
card.instruction: Seek signs that your contribution still earns a place. Increase your effort whenever belonging feels uncertain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep me in the quiz team. I've learned every capital we missed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to justify coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll learn the currencies as a bonus.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We like your company.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll make my company useful in two rounds instead of one.

card.title: Make the Win Count
card.instruction: Treat success as meaningless unless its difficulty, sacrifice, and personal cost are fully recognized.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you announce my cake won, mention I iced it at three in the morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ribbon says first prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ribbon got eight hours' sleep. It doesn't tell the full story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I mention the ingredients too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the ones I drove across town for after midnight.

card.title: Make the Win Count
card.instruction: Treat success as meaningless unless its difficulty, sacrifice, and personal cost are fully recognized.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, we finished first. Please tell them whose weekend disappeared into that presentation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone worked hard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. My hard work includes a cancelled anniversary dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want that in the speech?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before the applause, while people still have room to appreciate it.

transfer.action: I quietly remove the obstacle in front of {prop}.
transfer.opening: Another little advantage I won't mention again. {request}
transfer.response: Your smooth road has taken a lot of my effort. {counter}
transfer.challenge: Stop helping if you resent it.
transfer.closing: Then leave that hurdle there long enough to notice who usually moves it.

transfer.action: I write a new IOU beside the score for {prop}.
transfer.opening: That result changes what you owe me. {request}
transfer.response: The score carries forward in favours. {counter}
transfer.closing: Exactly. Today is an excellent day for collecting on it.

transfer.action: I move the finish marker farther from {prop}.
transfer.opening: This doesn't mean much if you stop playing. {request}
transfer.response: I'd rather keep the rivalry than collect the prize. {counter}
transfer.closing: And lose the person who makes the result interesting?

transfer.action: I unfold the years-old disputed score beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: This isn't new until the old point is settled. {request}
transfer.response: We've still never agreed where that coin landed. {counter}
transfer.closing: An impressively long delay for something you keep calling a small point.

transfer.action: I copy your winner's pose while presenting {prop}.
transfer.opening: I'll look that relaxed when mine is bigger. {request}
transfer.response: Watch me do it without breaking a sweat. {counter}
transfer.challenge: You're working very hard to seem relaxed.
transfer.closing: Only because I'm attempting a higher standard of effortlessness.

transfer.action: I place my best-season leaderboard beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: This is the record that tells the whole story. {request}
transfer.response: Give me the conditions that measured me properly. {counter}
transfer.closing: Then today hasn't yet received a fair chance to resemble my best year.

transfer.action: I move my smaller medal into the brightest light beside {prop}.
transfer.response: You can still see me from over there, right? {counter}
transfer.closing: Then keep my name in the sentence after the winner's.

transfer.action: I lay my repair bill beside the risky choice about {prop}.
transfer.opening: Your gamble keeps arriving on my account. {request}
transfer.response: I want a vote in consequences I pay for. {counter}
transfer.closing: Then find a way for the invoice to recognize your independence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancel your camping contest so my lawn doesn't pay for thirty tents. Show me you're on my side.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd lose the entry fee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. That's one consequence finally landing beside the decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Isn't that a harsh loyalty test?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then offer a real sacrifice that doesn't grow back in my garden.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A requests a costly loyalty gesture because B's risky choice otherwise lands costs on A; the requested sacrifice makes A's vote concrete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give up your first turn teaching the dog to fetch glasses. I buy the glasses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Training matters to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let protecting my budget matter enough to cost you a turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said I'd clean up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking for loyalty before the breakage, not help sweeping my share afterwards.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A requests a costly loyalty gesture because B's risky choice otherwise lands costs on A; the requested sacrifice makes A's vote concrete.

beats.text: Before you teach the dog to fetch glasses, can I vote? I buy the glasses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my training experiment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And my experiment is making rent after the breakages.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll clean up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Include replacing the glasses in your definition of clean.

card.title: Lose Something for Me
card.instruction: Create a loyalty test by asking them to accept a real disadvantage on your behalf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you give me your first turn, even if it costs you the match?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why would I do that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said you were on my side. This side has a cost.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant emotionally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lend the emotion a turn so I can see it.

card.title: Your Risk, My Cost
card.instruction: Treat every choice around you as a risk whose consequences may land on you. Press for a voice in decisions you cannot control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're inviting thirty people to camp in our garden? I maintain the lawn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only one weekend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Grass experiences time differently. I want a say in tent placement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making this complicated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm trying to keep your simple weekend out of my next six Saturdays.

card.title: Lose Something for Me
card.instruction: Create a loyalty test by asking them to accept a real disadvantage on your behalf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Miss the prize ceremony and come to my tiny opening night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm receiving the prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Coming wouldn't mean much if you had nothing else to do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's an unfair test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Maybe. I'm trying to discover whether I'm more than the convenient option.

transfer.action: I put another completed task beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: That's another reason to keep my seat. {request}
transfer.response: I can still make myself worth the space. {counter}
transfer.challenge: You don't need to earn every place.
transfer.closing: Then let me finish this one thing while I learn to believe that.

transfer.action: I put a bandage and the sleepless-hour tally beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: The result doesn't show what it cost me. {request}
transfer.response: Read the sacrifice as well as the score. {counter}
transfer.closing: The trophy didn't give up its weekend. I'd like that part named too.
